citations.quote:
Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a nonempty compact smooth embedded surface, possibly disconnected and nonorientable, every component of which has nonempty boundary. The ambient sphere has its standard orientation. The normal-transfer expression $B_F([a],[b])=\operatorname{lk}(a,\tau b)$ defines a symmetric integral bilinear pairing on the free finite-rank group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, with rational extension. It restricts on each component to its normal-transfer pairing; for cycles $a,b$ on distinct components its value is $2\operatorname{lk}(a,b)$, which need not vanish.

Suppose an embedded product cylinder $W=[-1,1]\times D^2$ meets $F$ exactly in its two end disks, on distinct components. Replace those disks by the lateral annulus and round the seams to obtain $F'$. There is an integral basis in which $B_{F'}$ has matrix $G\oplus[0]$, where $G$ is the entire matrix of $B_F$, including its cross-component entries. Thus its signature is unchanged. The boundary link and its surface collar remain fixed, so $e(F)=-\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i')$, computed from boundary normal push-offs, is unchanged as well.

A finite sequence of such tubes exists making $F$ connected. All intermediate surfaces still have the original boundary link and collar, no closed components, and finite smooth disk-and-band presentations on their components. The signature and $e$ are preserved throughout.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be an
oriented link with $r\ge1$ components and complement $X_L$,
([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]), and let
$$\varphi:H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z$$
be the **total linking homomorphism**, defined as the composite
$$H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow[\ \sim\ ]{\mathrm{Alex}}\widetilde H^1(L;\mathbb Z)\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^rH^1(K_i;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\text{sum}}\mathbb Z,$$
where the first arrow is Alexander duality
([[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]]),
each $H^1(K_i;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is the orientation-induced
identification, and the last map sums the $r$ coordinates. By
[[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]] the map $\varphi$
may again be written $\pi_1(X_L)\to H_1(X_L)\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathbb Z$; we
denote both composites by $\varphi$ and set $K:=\ker\varphi$.

The **one-variable Alexander module** of $L$ is
$$A_L:=H_1(\widetilde{X_L};\mathbb Z),$$
the first singular homology of the connected infinite cyclic cover
$p:\widetilde{X_L}\to X_L$ classified by $K$
([[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]],
[[lem-subgroup-quotient-of-universal-cover]],
[[def-covering-map-and-evenly-covered-neighbourhoods]]), equipped with its
structure of module over $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) in which $t$ acts by the deck
transformation corresponding to the positive generator of
$\operatorname{Deck}(\widetilde{X_L}/X_L)\cong\mathbb Z$.

**Caveats.** The cover is the one classified by $K=\ker\varphi$; since $K$ is
normal the cover is regular and its deck group is
$\pi_1(X_L)/K\cong\mathbb Z$
([[def-regular-covering]], [[thm-regular-covering-characterizations]], [[cor-deck-group-of-a-regular-covering]],
[[def-deck-transformation-and-deck-group]]). The module $A_L$ is ordinary
integral homology of the cover, with the deck action as its module structure;
no twisting by a representation of the link group is used. The total linking
homomorphism satisfies $\varphi(\mu_i)=1$ for a meridian $\mu_i$ of any one
component, so $r\ge1$ is needed for $\varphi$ to be interesting and $A_L$
depends on the orientations of all components through this map.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be the ordered integral basis and positive normal push-off convention used to define the Seifert matrix $V$ above. Every class of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ has a representative that is a finite integral sum of pairwise disjoint smooth oriented embedded circles in $F$. For such representatives $x$ and $y$, the sum of the pairwise linking numbers between the positive push-off of $x$ and $y$ depends only on $[x]$ and $[y]$, is independent of the sufficiently small positive push-off, and equals the bilinear extension of $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The linking number of two disjoint oriented circle components is symmetric. In particular, the Seifert pairing is a well-defined bilinear map $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$.

Assume full AC. Let $F_+,F_-\subset S^3$ be compact smooth embedded spanning surfaces for the same nonempty link $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_m$, with no closed components. The surfaces may be disconnected and nonorientable. Suppose the full rational normal-transfer pairing of $F_+$ is positive definite and that of $F_-$ is negative definite. Include cross-component entries in both pairings. Let $b_1(F)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_1(F;\mathbb Q)$, and define the total boundary slope by $s(F)=\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i^F)$, where $K_i^F$ is an inward push in the boundary collar of $F$, oriented compatibly with any orientation of $K_i$. Then
$$s(F_+)-s(F_-)=2\bigl(b_1(F_+)+b_1(F_-)\bigr).$$
The inward pushes can be replaced by surface-normal pushes without changing the slope. No link primeness or connectedness hypothesis is imposed, and a zero-dimensional definite form is allowed.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

derivations.claim: Push $K_i$ a little inward on a boundary collar, obtaining a two-sided interior curve $a_i$ on either surface. Transporting the collar and its short transverse normal fields from $K_i$ to $a_i$ is an isotopy of the disjoint curve-and-push pair. The two opposite normal pushes of $a_i$ have the same self-linking: a constant half-turn in the oriented normal disk plane homotopes one push to the other without crossing $a_i$. By [F2] each therefore has linking $f_i(F)$ with $a_i$. Thus [F1] gives $B_F([a_i],[a_i])=2f_i(F)$. A positive definite form has nonnegative value on every class, including zero, and a negative definite form has nonpositive value. This proves $f_i(F_+)\ge0\ge f_i(F_-)$ and $d_i\ge0$. Summing the component framing differences and applying [F3] proves the displayed equation.

Make coordinates on a boundary tube adapted to the actual collar of $F_-$. Extend that collar parametrization $c(s,u)$ a little across $u=0$ and take its short surface-normal push by $v$. The map $(s,u,v)\mapsto c(s,u)+v n(s,u)$, interpreted in a smooth ambient chart or its normal exponential map, has independent derivatives at $u=v=0$. By [F4] and compactness it is a smooth tube chart at sufficiently small uniform radius. Local extensions across the boundary may be patched outside the given collar using finite chart cutoffs before shrinking; on the positive $u$-ray the prescribed collar is retained. Choose the $v$ direction so the normal plane orientation agrees with that induced from the oriented $K_i$. Its angle-zero longitude has self-linking $f_i(F_-)$, because the inward collar push and the normal push differ by a fixed quarter-turn. On a short collar of $F_+$ the base projection is a coordinate and the normal radius is a strictly increasing inward parameter, as its derivative there is positive at the boundary; compactness and [F4] give these assertions on a uniform strip. Its collar therefore has coordinates $(s,r,\theta_i(s,r))$.

A transverse vector field along $K_i$ in this tube determines an angle map to the circle. On a cut parameter interval its real lift changes by $2\pi k$ for an integer $k$. Its pushed curve is homologous on the torus to the angle-zero longitude plus $k$ positive meridians: subtract its linear angle of degree $k$, leaving a periodic angle function which contracts to a constant by interpolation. Thus [F2] evaluates its self-linking as $f_i(F_-)+k$. Apply this to the inward tangent of $F_+$, whose framing equals its normal framing by a quarter-turn. Its relative winding is consequently $d_i$. The angle of its short collar has this same degree at every small $r$. First interpolate it on a smaller radius strip to its limiting angle at $r=0$, cutting off before the outer collar edge. Then interpolate that limit to $2\pi d_i s+\delta_i$ using a periodic lift of their difference. This difference is periodic precisely because their degrees agree. Keep $s,r$ fixed throughout. The maps remain embedded because distinct $(s,r)$ remain distinct, and they extend smoothly across $r=0$ as rotations by smooth periodic angles of the inward vector. They agree with the old embedding outside the tube collar and fix every point of $L$. By [F4] the finitely many collar isotopies extend to ambient isotopies fixing $L$. In the innermost tubes the resulting actual collar has exactly the asserted angle. The comparison surface is retained at its original position when making this comparison.

On a small $T_i$ the curves now are $(s,\theta)=(s,2\pi d_i s+\delta_i)$ and $(s,0)$. If $d_i=0$ they are disjoint. If $d_i>0$, the equation $2\pi d_i s+\delta_i=0\pmod{2\pi}$ has exactly $d_i$ solutions on $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$. Their tangent determinants in the positively ordered coordinates $(s,\theta)$ are $\det((1,2\pi d_i),(1,0))=-2\pi d_i$, proving transversality and the stated common sign. For any transverse representatives of these two slope classes, their algebraic intersection is still $-d_i$: the torus longitude and positive meridian form its oriented homology basis, their intersection is one, and bilinearity gives the same determinant of the two integral classes. This can also be read by lifting their angle difference to the cut interval; its signed zero count is its winding. Geometric intersection number is at least the absolute algebraic intersection, so $d_i$ is minimal. All the constructions preserved the full surface and component scope in the Statement.

boundaries.reason: A nonempty boundary link and spanning surfaces without closed components are assumed.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement allows zero first Betti number and zero signature; no inverse of the normal form is taken.
The Statement allows a one-component link and connected or disconnected surfaces satisfy the same argument.
The Statement uses the signature, which is the difference of positive and negative ranks; the proof does not require nonsingularity.
The Statement retains the same literal boundary link, with arbitrary component orientations.
The Statement explicitly assumes full AC, which is assumed and inherited through the cited linking and smooth construction suppliers.

axioms.use: Full AC is inherited from normal-transfer linking and the slope equation. It supplies countable choice for the compact supported isotopy extension. All boundary components and coordinate constructions are finite.

risk_review.notes: Preserves full disconnected and nonorientable surface scope. All new prerequisite sources and their geometric constructions still require independent owner review.
